[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Understand your camera's limits regarding ISO range and performance.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Use a lens with a wide aperture (like f/1.4 or f/2.8) to let more light in.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Shoot in RAW format for more flexibility in post-processing.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Keep ISO as low as possible (preferably 1600 or below) to minimize noise.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Use a tripod to stabilize the camera for slower shutter speeds.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 6. Slow down shutter speed to let more light in and create a sense of motion.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 7. Open up the aperture to let more light in and create a shallow depth of field.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 8. Use the camera's built-in noise reduction features.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 9. Shoot in burst mode to capture sharper images with less noise.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 10. Use noise reduction tools in editing software like Adobe Lightroom.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 11. Pay attention to available light sources for depth and interest.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 12. Experiment with different angles and compositions.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Additional tips include avoiding overexposure, using autofocus assist light, and considering a remote shutter release.
